title: Indian Intelligence Warns of Possible Pakistani 'LoC Misadventure' to Divert From PoK Unrest
detail: Anonymous Indian Intelligence Bureau officials, cited in an IANS wire report published September 10, 2026 and syndicated across several Indian outlets, said Pakistan's military — facing a wave of unrest in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) that has paralysed Rawalakot, Bhimber, Mirpur, Neelum Valley and Muzaffarabad with sit-ins and strikes called by the banned Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) — may attempt a 'major misadventure' along the Line of Control to distract from the crisis. The officials said the diversion could take the form of a skirmish requiring an Indian military response, or a major infiltration push timed to coincide with one, and linked the assessment to Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir 'facing heat internally' over his handling of the PoK protests and violence in Balochistan. The same officials said the ISI has a 'desperate need... to recruit youth in J&K and get them to undertake acts of terror,' and that Indian security agencies are in a 'state of very high alert' along the LoC as a result. No actual LoC firing, infiltration attempt or other incident had occurred as of September 11, and neither Pakistan's government nor military issued any public response to the claims.

media.caption: Reporting on Indian intelligence assessments of a possible Pakistani LoC diversion amid PoK unrest, September 10, 2026

confidenceReason: Single IANS wire report attributed to anonymous Intelligence Bureau officials, syndicated across multiple Indian outlets (Hans India, Punjab Kesari and others) rather than independently reported; no on-record Indian government confirmation, no Pakistani response, and no actual LoC incident occurred as of Sep 11 — an intelligence assessment/prediction, not a confirmed event.

title: Satellite Imagery Reportedly Shows Pakistan Expanding Electronic Warfare Sites Near LoC and in Sindh
detail: Indian Defence News reported September 10, 2026, based on satellite imagery, that Pakistan has expanded electronic warfare (EW) and electronic support measures (ESM) infrastructure at two sites: Dadyal in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, roughly 33 km from the Line of Control, and PAF Base Sindhri in Mirpur Khas, Sindh, where new EW-related equipment was identified near hardened aircraft shelters supporting electronic and signals intelligence (ELINT/SIGINT) functions. The report characterised the buildup as part of a 'networked electronic warfare grid' combining forward LoC-area surveillance nodes with base-level ELINT infrastructure, describing it as paralleling India's own electronic-warfare investments. The assessment rests on commercial satellite-imagery interpretation by a specialist defence-news outlet; it has not been confirmed by Indian or Pakistani officials and no other outlet has independently corroborated the specific site details.

media.caption: Satellite-imagery-based reporting on Pakistani electronic warfare infrastructure near Dadyal, PoK, September 2026

confidenceReason: Single specialist defence-news outlet's interpretation of commercial satellite imagery; no official Indian or Pakistani confirmation and no corroborating Tier-1/2 outlet identified.
